blocks.text: This chapter is the practical guide to the Shaddad UGV digital twin. It takes a new engineer from a fresh MATLAB session to a completed Phase 1 test drive, explains the options of the run scripts, shows where the results are stored and how to read them, and lists the known pitfalls of the reference PC. Every command, function and option in this chapter exists in the project as delivered on 2026-10-23. Type the commands in the MATLAB Command Window. Paths are relative to the project root unless stated otherwise. Commands write the project root as `<project root>`: the folder that holds `Shaddad_UGV.prj` ({sec:ch08_user_manual/Getting the project}; `C:\Users\aomar\Desktop\Robot project` on the reference PC).
Quick start
Four commands cover the normal Phase 1 workflow:

openProject('<project root>\Shaddad_UGV.prj');   % load data, print the startup report
res = phase1_test_drive();      % default RC demo drive with summary, figure, replay (about 4-5 min)
r1  = run_scenario('S1');       % RC drive acceptance scenario, 120 s simulated (about 5-6 min)
rt  = run_regression('Fast');   % fast static regression checks (about 1-3 min)

**Expected result of `run_regression('Fast')`**: 24 tests, 22 pass and 2 fail. The two failures, `t_infra` testStartup and testPlantStructure, are stale test expectations, not model defects ({tab:tab_regr_fail}). This is the result of the last run on the model after the fix pass (2026-10-23 23:31, report `work/reports/Fast_20261023_233144`). Any other failure is a real problem.
Run everything in Normal simulation mode, which is the default of every script. On the reference PC, Windows Application Control blocks the MEX files that Accelerator and Rapid Accelerator generate.
Prerequisites
MATLAB release and required products

The model is built and verified with MATLAB R2026b (26.2) on Windows 11. Older releases are not supported, because the build scripts use R2026b block libraries and the models are saved by R2026b. {tab:tab_products} lists the products that the simulation needs and where the model uses them.

blocks.text: PC requirements

items: Windows 11, 64-bit, with 16 GB RAM (reference PC). Treat 16 GB as the minimum.

Each compile of `Shaddad_System` grows the MATLAB process by about 0.5-1 GB, and the memory is not released. Above about 9 GB the PC pages and runs 4-5 times slower (Normal-mode RTF 0.12 instead of about 0.49). Restart MATLAB before it reaches that level.
In Normal mode the Phase 1 real-time factor (RTF) is about 0.3-0.5, so one simulated second takes 2-3 s of execution time plus the model compile.
Disk space: `work/` holds the model cache and the results. One default test-drive log is about 25 MB.

blocks.text: Check the MATLAB memory use at any time:
m = memory;  fprintf('MATLAB uses %.1f GB\n', m.MemUsedMATLAB/1e9);
Getting the project

The digital twin is delivered as one folder, `Robot project`, that holds the MATLAB project file `Shaddad_UGV.prj`. This folder is the **project root**; the commands in this report write it as `<project root>`. On the reference PC it is `C:\Users\aomar\Desktop\Robot project`. It is not a Git repository on the reference PC, and the official NASL storage location for releases is still to be fixed [TBD - NASL project owner: repository or file-share location]. To set it up on another PC:

items: Copy (or clone, once a repository exists) the complete `Robot project` folder to a local disk, for example `D:\Shaddad\Robot project`. Keep the folder structure: `Shaddad_UGV.prj`, `resources/`, `models/`, `subsystems/`, `params/`, `buses/`, `scripts/`, `utilities/`, `tests/`, `docs/` and `+bus_conv_fcns/` must stay together. `work/` (about 1 GB of caches and logs on the reference PC) is regenerated and need not be copied; copy `work/results/` only if you want the saved runs of this report. The project defines `work/` as its Simulink cache and code-generation folder, so if you do not copy it, create an empty `work/` folder in the project root before `openProject` (`mkdir work`).
Start MATLAB R2026b and open the project, either with the full path or from the project root (the commands below).

Check the startup report against {tab:tab_startup}. The models are delivered built: `models/` contains all 8 models and `subsystems/` the 117 referenced model files, so no `build_*` script is needed before the first run. Rebuild only after you change a build script ({sec:ch08_user_manual/Regenerating models}).

blocks.text: Opening the project
openProject('<project root>\Shaddad_UGV.prj');
Opening the project puts the project folders on the MATLAB path and runs the registered startup file `scripts/shaddad_startup.m`, which performs these steps:

items: Starts the Simulink product. This costs time only on first use in a MATLAB process (8-18 s on the reference PC) and is timed separately.

Runs `shaddad_params()`. It creates the parameter struct `P`, the sample-time struct `Ts`, the descriptive strings `P_meta`, the 13 variant controls `VC_*` and the 88 `Bus_*` objects in the base workspace.
Runs `shaddad_configsets('fixed')`. It creates the configuration sets `cs_*`. `cs_Shaddad`, which every model references, receives the fixed-step settings (ode3, 1 ms).
Creates the Phase 2 row-tracker MPC object `mpcRowObj` with `gnc_designMPC` when `VC_ROW_TRACKER == 1`.
Prints the product and tool report ({tab:tab_startup}).
Sets the Simulation Data Inspector to automatic archiving with a limit of 10 runs (`P.log.sdi_archive_runs`), so memory stays bounded during batches.

blocks.text: The startup never changes the current folder and never runs `clear all`, `close all` or `bdclose all`. Its time budget is 15 s, not counting the Simulink product start. Repeat it in a running session, or restore every default after an experiment, with:

rep = shaddad_startup();      % prints the report; rep.table holds it as a MATLAB table
shaddad_startup('quiet');     % same, without printing
shaddad_shutdown();           % removes P, Ts, P_meta, mpcRowObj, VC_*, Bus_*, cs_*

blocks.text: Startup leaves these variables in the base workspace: the parameter struct `P`, the sample times `Ts` and the strings `P_meta` ({tab:tab_params}), the 13 variant controls `VC_*` with the defaults in {tab:tab_vc_arch}, the 88 `Simulink.Bus` objects `Bus_*` (`shaddad_buses`), the configuration sets `cs_SimFixed`, `cs_SimRef`, `cs_GenARM`, `cs_STM32H7`, `cs_STM32G4`, `cs_Companion` and `cs_Shaddad` (`shaddad_configsets`; every model references `cs_Shaddad`) and the Phase 2 MPC object `mpcRowObj` (`gnc_designMPC`).

The scenario scripts set the variant controls they need through `Simulink.SimulationInput` (`scn_base_input`), so a scenario run never changes the base workspace. A run of `Shaddad_System` started from the Simulink editor uses the base-workspace values.
Exploring the model in Simulink

After the startup you can open the models in the Simulink editor to see how the twin is built. {sec:ch02_architecture/Top model and model hierarchy} explains the hierarchy; {fig:F01_system_top_overview.png} and {fig:F17_simulink_editor_callouts.png} show the top model, and the callout numbers are those of {tab:tab_top}.

open_system('Shaddad_System');               % top model
open_system('Shaddad_System/Operator_RC');   % a Subsystem Reference (subsystems/rc/RC_Link_Sim.slx)
open_system('Shaddad_MCU');                  % a referenced model on its own
close_system('Shaddad_System', 0);           % close without saving

items: **Move down the hierarchy.** Double-click the Model blocks `MCU`, `BMS` or `Plant` to open the referenced models `Shaddad_MCU`, `Shaddad_BMS` and `Shaddad_Plant`. A Subsystem Reference, for example `Operator_RC` or `Power_Plant`, opens like a normal subsystem; its content comes from its file in `subsystems/<domain>/`. The address bar above the canvas shows the current path; click an entry in it to go back up.
**Model Browser.** Show it with the Hide/Show Model Browser button at the lower-left corner of the canvas. Its tree lists the subsystems of the open model; click an entry to open it.

**Active variants.** The Variant Subsystems and Variant Sources (for example `GNC_Variant`, the `IO_In` / `IO_Out` blocks of the MCU and the pack and drive-plant variants) follow the `VC_*` values in the base workspace ({tab:tab_vc_arch}). After an update of the diagram (Ctrl+D, which compiles the model) the inactive choices are greyed out. On the **Debug** tab, **Information Overlays > Variant Legend** lists the variant controls with their current values and conditions.

blocks.text: Never save a model from the editor: every `.slx` file is generated, so change the build script instead ({tab:tab_build}).
Project folder map

{fig:F33_project_structure.png} shows the folder tree and {tab:tab_folders_arch} lists what each folder contains ({sec:ch02_architecture/Project and file structure}). The folders you use most as a model user:

items: `scripts/`: the entry points `phase1_test_drive.m`, `run_scenario.m` and `run_all_scenarios.m`; `scripts/scenarios/` holds the scenario definitions `scn_S0` to `scn_S8`, `scn_D1_test_drive.m` and the shared helpers (`scn_base_input.m`, `scn_rc_tab.m`); `scripts/build/` the 39 model generators `build_*.m`; `scripts/missions/` the Phase 2 mission files.
`params/`: `shaddad_params.m`, the 9 files `param_<domain>.m` and `shaddad_configsets.m` ({sec:ch08_user_manual/Changing parameters}).
`subsystems/<domain>/`: the 117 referenced model files and the state-machine functions `esc_sm.m`, `mcu_mode_manager.m` and `sbus_frame_sync.m`.
`tests/<domain>/`: 18 `matlab.unittest` classes, the benches `tb_*.slx` and `tests/run_regression.m` ({sec:ch08_user_manual/Running tests}).

`work/`: generated at run time: model cache (`slprj`, `*.slxc`), `results/` (run logs), `reports/` (test reports). `resources/` is the project metadata and `+bus_conv_fcns/` holds the ROS 2 bus conversion functions; do not edit either.

blocks.text: Every `.slx` file in `models/` and `subsystems/` is generated by a script in `scripts/build/`. Never edit a model by hand in the Simulink editor: the next build overwrites the change, and the model no longer matches its script. Change the build script and regenerate ({tab:tab_build}).
Running the Phase 1 test drive

`phase1_test_drive` is the main demonstration entry point. It drives the robot with the simulated RC transmitter through the complete Phase 1 chain: transmitter, SBUS bytes on the UART line, the STM32 SBUS decoder and RC mapping, the MCU mode manager and vehicle control, CAN to the two ESCs, the PMSM motors and 24:1 gearboxes, and the tracks on soil, all powered by the 48 V pack under BMS control. Internally it calls `run_scenario('D1', ..., 'Mode', 'normal')` with the scenario `scripts/scenarios/scn_D1_test_drive.m`. It then prints a summary, draws a results figure and plays the bird's-eye replay.
Syntax and options
`phase1_test_drive` takes the name-value options in {tab:tab_d1_options}:

res = phase1_test_drive()                                    % default demo drive (64 s simulated)
res = phase1_test_drive('Plan', plan)                        % your own maneuver, plan = N x 3 [t v w]
res = phase1_test_drive(..., 'EStopAt', 20, 'ResetAt', 25)   % remote E-stop (CH12) and reset (CH9)
res = phase1_test_drive(..., 'RCLoss', [20 23])              % RF link lost from 20 s to 23 s
res = phase1_test_drive(..., 'World', 1, 'Implement', 0, 'StopTime', T, 'Replay', true)

blocks.caption: Options of phase1_test_drive
rows: N x 3 maneuver table `[t v w]`
Time [s] at which the remote E-stop switch CH12 is thrown
Time [s] at which the reset button CH9 is pressed. Must be at least `EStopAt` + 1.5 s. Without it the E-stop stays latched until the end.
`[t_loss t_back]`: the RF link is lost and restored
World id 1-6: flat_test, slope_test, palm_farm, greenhouse, solar_farm, soil_strips. This report uses world 1 only.
0 none, 1 mower, 2 tiller, 3 sprayer (`VC_IMPL`). The implement is mounted; its switch CH8 stays OFF.
Last plan or event time + 8 s
Play the bird's-eye replay after the run

blocks.text: The scenario's input parser rejects any other option. The simulation mode is always Normal.
The maneuver plan

Each plan row `[t v w]` means: from time `t` [s], hold the forward speed `v` [m/s] and the yaw rate `w` [rad/s] until the next row. Signs: `v > 0` drives forward and `w > 0` turns left (counter-clockwise seen from above). A row with `v = 0` and `w` not zero is a pivot turn on the spot. Rows are sorted by time, and a `[0 0 0]` row is added when the first row starts after 0 s. The manual limits are |v| ≤ 2.0 m/s and |w| ≤ 1.0 rad/s (`P.electronics.lim.v_max_man`, `P.electronics.lim.w_max_man`).

The plan does not go to the controller directly. `scn_rc_stick` converts each `v` and `w` into the transmitter stick position for which the MCU RC mapping decodes exactly that value; it inverts the deadband, the expo curve and the speed knob (set to 100 %). The MCU then treats the command like real operator input. It accelerates at up to 0.8 m/s², brakes at up to 1.2 m/s², and caps the yaw-rate reference at `a_lat_max/max(|v|, 0.1 m/s)` with `a_lat_max` = 1.0 m/s² (`P.electronics.lim.v_lat_min` = 0.1 m/s), so a pivot turn is limited by `w_max_man`. A step to 1.2 m/s therefore reaches 90 % of the target in about 1.5 s.

`phase1_test_drive` switches MATLAB warnings off during the run. A plan value outside the limits is clipped to the limit without a visible warning. Check the plan against the limits before you run it.

The scenario adds a fixed operator sequence around the plan: transmitter on at 0.5 s, arm switch (CH6) on at 2 s with the sticks neutral, speed knob at 100 % and mode switch at MANUAL. {tab:tab_d1_plan} lists the default plan.

blocks.caption: Default demo maneuver of phase1_test_drive
rows: Power-up, arm at 2 s, stand still
Stop; the run ends at 64 s

blocks.text: Examples
**Custom plan.** Accelerate to 1.0 m/s at 4 s, add a left arc at 15 s and stop at 25 s. The run ends at 33 s.

plan = [0 0 0;  4 1.0 0;  15 1.0 0.4;  25 0 0];
res = phase1_test_drive('Plan', plan);

**Remote E-stop and recovery.** CH12 is thrown at 20 s, the MCU enters ESTOP and stops the robot with the E-stop deceleration profile. The scenario then performs the operator recovery listed in {tab:tab_d1_events}, and the plan resumes.
res = phase1_test_drive('EStopAt', 20, 'ResetAt', 25);

**RC link loss.** The RF link is lost from 20 s to 23 s. The MCU declares RC_LINK_LOST 0.10 s after the last valid frame and makes a controlled stop, not an E-stop. After the link returns, the robot stays stopped until the arm switch is cycled.
res = phase1_test_drive('RCLoss', [20 23]);

blocks.caption: Operator actions that the test drive adds automatically
rows: Sticks neutral from te; CH12 back to RUN at tr - 1 s; reset button pressed from tr to tr + 0.3 s; arm off at tr + 2 s, on at tr + 3 s; plan resumes at tr + 4 s
CH12 stays at STOP and the sticks stay neutral until the end of the run
Link lost from t1 to t2; arm off at t2 + 4 s, on at t2 + 5 s; sticks neutral from t1 to t2 + 6 s

blocks.text: **Implement, fixed duration, no replay.** Options can be combined:

res = phase1_test_drive('Implement', 1);                  % mower mounted (VC_IMPL 1)
res = phase1_test_drive('Plan', plan, 'StopTime', 40);    % fixed simulated duration
res = phase1_test_drive('Replay', false);                 % summary and figure only
The same scenario runs without figure and replay through the scenario runner: `res = run_scenario('D1', 'Args', {'Plan', plan});`.

blocks.text: Reading the figure
{fig:F23_d1_dashboard.png} shows the results figure of the default drive. The panels are:

blocks.caption: Results figure of the default test drive D1 (2026-10-23 20:11, 64 s simulated in 251 s, RTF 0.44, Normal mode): RC command at the MCU against the true forward speed (max 1.19 m/s) and yaw rate, the 34.8 m path, left and right track belt speeds, and the pack current with the MCU mode (BOOT -> SELFTEST -> STANDBY -> MANUAL at 2.04 s).

items: **Forward speed** (top left): the speed target that the MCU decoded from the RC sticks (`telem.v_target`, stairs) and the true forward speed (`truth.speed_fwd`). The true speed follows each step along the ramp of the MCU shaper.
**Yaw rate** (top right): the RC yaw-rate target (`telem.w_target`) and the true body yaw rate (`truth.omega_B`, z component), positive to the left.
**Path on the field** (left, two rows high): the true position East/North (`truth.pos_W`) with the start (green) and the end (red), equal axis scaling.
**Track belt speeds** (middle right): left and right belt speeds (`truth.vBelt_LR`). Equal speeds mean straight driving, different speeds a turn, opposite signs a pivot turn.
**Battery current and MCU mode** (bottom right): the pack current (`power_truth.I_pack_A`, left axis) and the MCU mode (right axis, BOOT to FAULT).

blocks.text: In the default drive, speed and yaw rate follow the commands within 0.025 m/s and 0.011 rad/s in every segment ({tab:tab_d1_track}, {sec:ch09_results/Demonstration drive (D1)}).
Bird's-eye replay

After the figure, `shaddad_replay_birdseye(res.file)` plays the run as a top view in 0.1 s frames ({fig:F24_d1_birdseye.png}). It shows the world map, the robot footprint at its true pose and the trail. The title line gives the time, the MCU mode, the SOC and the position-estimate error; the estimate error is meaningful in Phase 2 only. LiDAR returns are not stored in the log, so the replay shows none.

blocks.caption: Bird's-eye replay of D1 (`shaddad_replay_birdseye`), final frame at t = 64.1 s: the 34.8 m driven path from the origin and the vehicle footprint at the end point. The |e_pos| field in the title compares truth with the navigation estimate, which Phase 1 does not compute (GNC_Stub), so it has no meaning here.

blocks.text: Replay any saved run later:

shaddad_replay_birdseye(res.file);                            % this run
shaddad_replay_birdseye(res.file, 'Step', 5);                 % every 5th frame (faster)
shaddad_replay_birdseye(res.file, 'Video', 'd1_drive.mp4');   % also write an MP4 video
shaddad_replay_birdseye(res.file, 'Pause', 0.05);             % slow the replay down
shaddad_replay_birdseye(res.file, 'Visible', false, 'Video', 'd1.mp4');   % video only
shaddad_replay_birdseye();                                    % latest S*.mat (not D1)
Log file and wall time

Each run is saved as `work/results/D1_<yyyyMMdd_HHmmss>.mat` (MAT-file version 7.3, about 25 MB for the default drive). The path is in `res.file`. The file holds the result struct without the SimulationInput and SimulationOutput objects ({tab:tab_res}). The default 64 s drive (2026-10-23 20:11) took about 251 s of wall time on the reference PC in Normal mode (146 s execution plus compile), which is about 4 s of wall time per simulated second; the replay adds time, so plan about 4-5 min for `phase1_test_drive()`. The help text of the function still quotes 2-3 min; use the measured value for planning. A memory-loaded session is several times slower.
Running the predefined scenarios

The scenarios are the acceptance tests of the digital twin. Each script `scripts/scenarios/scn_<id>_*.m` returns a `Simulink.SimulationInput` with the operator, fault and environment tables, and a list of pass/fail criteria. `run_scenario` runs the simulation, evaluates the criteria and saves the result.
run_scenario
`run_scenario` takes the scenario id and the name-value options in {tab:tab_rs_options}:

r = run_scenario('S1');                             % RC drive, Normal mode, saved to work/results
r = run_scenario('S1', 'Mode', 'normal');           % explicit mode (default)
r = run_scenario('S1', 'StopTime', 20);             % short run: latencies and the first speed step
r = run_scenario('S6c');                            % trailing letter = variant
r = run_scenario('S8', 'Variant', 'a', 'Viz', 1);   % live bird's-eye view during the run
r = run_scenario('S0', 'Save', false);              % do not write a result file

rows: `'S0'` to `'S8'` with an optional variant letter (`'S6c'`, `'S8b'`); `'D1'` is the test drive
`'normal'`, `'accelerator'` or `'rapid'`. Use `'normal'` on the reference PC.
`VC_VIZ` for this run; 1 = live bird's-eye view (slower)
`'fixed'` = ode3, 1 ms. `'ref'` currently fails (open problem 12 in `docs/STATUS.md`).
Extra name-value pairs for the scenario script (used for D1)
Parameter struct to use instead of the base workspace
Wall-time guard [s]; when it fires the run stops with `stop_reason` 7
Operator tables and variant controls for an id without a scenario file (default input: key on, TX off, no faults)
Keep the SimulationOutput in `res.out`; `false` frees it (used by `run_all_scenarios`)

blocks.text: `run_scenario` sets `CaptureErrors` on, so a run that stops with an error still returns the logs up to the error. It retries the run once when R2026b raises the `Stateflow:Assertion o != nullptr` error on the first compile. The last line summarises the run:
run_scenario S1: normal, solver fixed, 120 s simulated, exec <s> s, wall <s> s (RTF <x>), ok=1, pass=1

blocks.text: D1, S0, S2, S6a, S6b and S8b were re-run on 2026-10-23 between 20:11 and 20:47; S1, S6c, S6d and S8a are the post-fix runs of 07:25-07:56 ({tab:tab_ph1_runs}). {sec:ch09_results} gives the criteria and plots of every run. The criterion `S1.rtf` is hard-coded BLOCKED with the stale text "no C compiler"; the measured Normal-mode RTF is in `r.rtf` (0.47). The Phase 2 scenarios S3 (4 h endurance), S4 (greenhouse), S5 (palm patrol) and S7 (GNSS dropout) are outside the scope of this report.
Running several scenarios

Do not run all nine Phase 1 scenarios in one MATLAB session, because MATLAB memory grows with every compile ({sec:ch08_user_manual/PC requirements}). Split the set into batches of at most four scenarios, each in a fresh MATLAB session, or use one scenario per session as in {sec:ch09_results/Provenance of the results}. On 2026-10-23 the nine scenarios and the D1 drive took about 39 min of `sim()` wall time in Normal mode, S2 alone about 12 min:

% one batch per fresh MATLAB session (restart MATLAB and reopen the project in between)
R1 = run_all_scenarios({'S0', 'S1', 'S6c', 'S6d'}, 'Parallel', false);   % about 11 min
R2 = run_all_scenarios({'S6a', 'S6b', 'S8a', 'S8b'}, 'Parallel', false);  % about 12 min
R3 = run_all_scenarios({'S2'}, 'Parallel', false);                        % about 12 min

Without arguments, `run_all_scenarios()` runs every scenario and variant except S3, including the long Phase 2 missions. Runs are grouped by world and variant set. With `'Parallel'` set to `'auto'` (default) the function uses `parsim` when Parallel Computing Toolbox (PCT) is licensed and installed and either a parallel pool exists or more than 8 GB of physical memory is free. When PCT is not installed or less than 8 GB is free it runs serially; pass `'Parallel', false` to force serial runs. Parallel Computing Toolbox is installed on the reference PC, so with `'auto'` and more than 8 GB of free memory `parsim` would start workers that each compile the model and need several GB of memory of their own; this has not been tried. It prints a table (id, group, ok, pass, RTF, wall time) and, with `'Save'` true (default), saves each run and `work/results/all_<time>.mat`. The `'Workers'` option (default 2) is accepted but not used by the current code.
Reading the criteria table
After the simulation, `eval_criteria` prints one row per criterion with its id, status, measured value, operator, limit with unit and description. An excerpt of S1 (values rounded):

criterion          status            value   op limit            description
S1.rise            PASS               1.51   <= 2 s              90 % speed rise time (target ...)
S1.stop_dist       PASS              0.844   <= 0.95 m           stop distance after throttle release ...
S1.rtf             BLOCKED             NaN   >= 5                RTF >= 5 in accelerator ... BLOCKED: ...

The metric could not be computed, for example because a signal is missing. Counts as not passed.

blocks.text: `r.pass` is true when the simulation ended without error (`r.ok`) and every criterion is PASS or BLOCKED. `r.eval` holds the same rows as a struct array; `struct2table(r.eval)` shows them in the Variables editor. When criteria code changes after a long run, `scn_reeval('S8a')` evaluates the latest saved result again without simulating.
Interactive driving with the dashboard

Interactive dashboard driving was not exercised in this session. The dashboard variant compiles in the variant-matrix test (T-INT-10), but no drive with it has been verified. In Normal mode the simulation runs at about 0.3-0.5 times real time, so the robot reacts to the controls with a visible delay and moves in slow motion.

With `VC_OPSRC = 2`, the Variant Source in `Shaddad_System/Operator_Console` takes the operator commands (`Bus_OperatorCmd`) from the `Dashboard` subsystem instead of the scenario table. The subsystem holds 15 Constant blocks, one per bus element, initialised from `P.scen.dash`, and eight Simulink dashboard blocks bound to them ({fig:F13_operator_console.png} in {sec:ch06_electronics/Operator Inputs and the Operator Console}, {tab:tab_dash}). Moving a control during the simulation changes the bound Constant, just as moving a stick or switch changes the channel on the real transmitter.

Procedure

items: Open the project, then prepare the base workspace and start the simulation:

blocks.text:
P = scn_integration_overrides(P);   % 4.7 Ohm precharge resistor, as in every scenario
VC_OPSRC = 2;                       % operator commands from the dashboard
VC_VIZ = 1;                         % optional: live bird's-eye view (time, mode, SOC)
set_param(cs_Shaddad, 'StopTime', '600');                   % 600 s simulated (default 10 s)
open_system('Shaddad_System/Operator_Console/Dashboard');
set_param('Shaddad_System', 'SimulationCommand', 'start');  % or press Run in the editor

items: Keep the sliders at 0 and wait until the MCU reaches STANDBY (about 1 s simulated). Expected: with `VC_VIZ = 1` the live-view title shows STANDBY; after the run, `S.telem.mode` is 2 (STANDBY) at this time.
With both sliders at 0, switch `Arm_switch` on. The rising edge arms the MCU, and the mode changes to MANUAL.
Move `Thr_slider` forward for speed and `Steer_slider` to turn (+ = right). `Speed_knob` scales both commands from 25 % to 100 %.
Return the sliders to 0 to stop. The MCU brakes at up to 1.2 m/s².
Remote E-stop: switch `Estop_switch` on. The robot stops and the ESTOP state latches. To recover, switch it off, press `Reset_button`, keep the sliders at 0, and switch `Arm_switch` off and on again.
Link-loss test: switch `TX_power` off. After 0.10 s without valid frames the MCU declares RC_LINK_LOST and makes a controlled stop. Switch it on again and cycle `Arm_switch` to continue.
Stop the simulation, collect the logs and restore the defaults.

blocks.text: Without `scn_integration_overrides`, the 22 Ω precharge resistor and the ESC idle load hold the DC bus at 87 % of the pack voltage, the BMS precharge check times out and HV_Ready never rises (open problem 10 in `docs/STATUS.md`). Every scenario applies the 4.7 Ω override automatically. The simulation output `out` is returned to the base workspace because the configuration sets have `ReturnWorkspaceOutputs` on.

The result struct
`phase1_test_drive` and `run_scenario` return the same result struct ({tab:tab_res}). Load a saved run with `r = load(file)`, or the latest run of a scenario with `[r, file] = scn_latest('S1')`.

blocks.text: Logged signal groups

`scn_collect` converts the logged Dataset into nested structs: `S.<group>.<element>.t` is the time vector and `.v` holds the data, one row per sample. The leaves keep their logged class (single, uint8, logical), so convert them with `double()` before arithmetic. The MCU mode in `telem.mode` is coded 0 BOOT, 1 SELFTEST, 2 STANDBY, 3 MANUAL, 4 HOLD, 5 AUTO_START, 6 AUTO, 7 CTRL_STOP, 8 ESTOP, 9 FAULT.

rows: Environment, structure diagnostics, raw sensors, scenario input

             S.drive_truth.R.T_winding.t, S.drive_truth.R.T_winding.v - 273.15); grid on

Simulation Data Inspector

The logged signals of each run are also available in the Simulation Data Inspector. The startup enables automatic archiving with a limit of 10 runs, so older runs drop out of the archive. Open it with `Simulink.sdi.view`, select the signals of the latest run in the signal tree, and compare two runs with the Compare tab. For a run that is still in memory, the same Dataset is in `res.out.logsout`.
Changing parameters

All numeric values of the model are in the parameter files `params/param_<domain>.m` ({tab:tab_param_files}). `shaddad_params` calls them in dependency order, assembles `P`, `Ts` and the variant controls, runs cross-domain consistency checks (for example sprocket radius, gear ratio, pack energy, GNC envelope against the MCU limits) and writes everything to the base workspace. Block parameters in the generated models are expressions of `P`, for example `P.electronics.lim.v_max_man`. A changed value therefore takes effect at the next simulation without regenerating the model, as long as it does not change a signal dimension, a sample time or the model structure.

blocks.text: For a one-off experiment, change the base-workspace struct directly. This works for the runs that read it:

Edit the file, not only `P`, whenever other values derive from the one you change. `param_power.m`, for example, computes the per-group initial SOC vector and the BMS initial SOC estimate from `pk.SOC0`; changing `P.power.pack.SOC0` in memory leaves those derived values unchanged.
Example: manual speed and yaw-rate limits
The limits are the struct `E.lim` in `params/param_electronics.m`:

E.lim = struct('v_max_man',2.0,'w_max_man',1.0,'v_max_auto',1.5,'v_rev_auto',0.5,'w_max_auto',1.2, ...
    'a_lat_max',1.0,'v_track_max',2.0,'v_overspeed',2.4,'t_overspeed',0.2);

`v_max_man` and `w_max_man` are the full-stick values of the RC mapping (`fw_rc_mapping`). Lowering them needs no rebuild: the same stick position then commands less, and `phase1_test_drive` clips plans to the new limits. Before you raise `v_max_man` above 2.0 m/s, also review the track speed limit `v_track_max` (2.0 m/s), the overspeed trip `v_overspeed` (2.4 m/s for 0.2 s), the ESC limits in `param_drive.m` and the S1 criteria.
Example: RC deadband and expo
The RC mapping curve is in the struct `rc` of `params/param_electronics.m` (`P.electronics.rcmap`):
rc.deadband = 0.05; rc.expo_thr = 0.20; rc.expo_steer = 0.35; rc.sw_thresh = 0.5;

The Dead Zone, Gain and Polynomial blocks of `fw_rc_mapping` use these values: the deadband as a fraction of half the stick travel, and the expo as the cubic share of the stick curve. No rebuild is needed. `scn_rc_stick` inverts the new curve automatically, so scenario plans still command the same speeds. The transmitter side of the link (frame period, failsafe presets, channel map) is in `param_rc.m`; keep its channel map identical to `rc.ch` in `param_electronics.m`.
Example: battery pack

To change the initial charge, set `pk.SOC0` in the pack section of `params/param_power.m` (default 0.95) and run `shaddad_params()`. The pack size is spread over several coupled values ({tab:tab_pack}); change them together.

Regenerating models

The build scripts in `scripts/build/` are idempotent: each one closes, deletes and regenerates its files from parameter expressions and the ICD port tables. Most of them need `P`, `Ts` and the `Bus_*` objects in the base workspace, which the startup provides. {tab:tab_build} lists the scripts that a model change typically needs.

build_drive({'esc'});                            % only drive_esc.slx (e.g. Torque_Limiter change)
build_drive();                                   % every drive file, in dependency order
build_shaddad_mcu('model');                      % only Shaddad_MCU.slx; the firmware units must exist
build_shaddad_plant(); build_shaddad_system();   % integration models

Do not run `build_shaddad_mcu()` or `build_shaddad_mcu('all')` (the no-argument default is `'all'`), or `build_fw_platform()` with its default list. All of them rebuild the MCU platform units and overwrite the five control units of build task T09 (mode manager, safety supervisor, vehicle control, implement aux, watchdog manager) with interface stubs. Rebuild single units by name instead, for example `build_fw_platform({'fw_sbus_decoder'})`.

The ESC and MCU state machines and the SBUS framer are plain MATLAB functions called from MATLAB Function blocks: `subsystems/drive/esc_sm.m` (ESC DS402 state machine), `subsystems/electronics/mcu_mode_manager.m` (MCU modes) and `subsystems/electronics/sbus_frame_sync.m` (SBUS frame synchronisation and rejection). A change in these files takes effect at the next compile without a rebuild. After any rebuild or logic change, run the tests of the domain and the S0 and S1 scenarios.
Running tests

rt = run_regression('Fast');                 % static checks (t_infra, t_framework), about 1-3 min
rt = run_regression('All');                  % every class: several hours (see below)
rt = runtests('tests/rc/t_rc_link.m');       % one test class
rt = runtests('t_infra', 'Tag', 'Fast');     % static checks of one class (< 1 min)
table(rt)                                    % results as a table

**Expected result of `run_regression('Fast')`**: 24 tests, 22 pass and 2 fail (`t_infra` testStartup and testPlantStructure, stale expectations, {tab:tab_regr_fail}). The last run on the model after the fix pass (2026-10-23 23:31, `work/reports/Fast_20261023_233144`, 1.0 min in a running session) gave exactly this result. Any other failure is a real problem. `run_regression('All')` runs for several hours; run the heavy classes one by one with a MATLAB restart in between ({sec:ch08_user_manual/PC requirements}).

`run_regression` writes an HTML report to `work/reports/<tag>_<time>` and a JUnit XML file next to it. The suite has 18 test classes in `tests/<domain>/`. At the 2026-10-23 acceptance, before the fix pass, it counted 391 tests: 328 passed, 31 failed, 30 incomplete and 2 not run. 12 of the 31 failures came from the two motion defects that the fix pass has since removed (these tests have not been re-run). About 13 are stale test expectations (`docs/STATUS.md` section 4.1), 3 are simulation-speed (RTF) targets and the rest are known open problems (R2026b assertion, reference solver, `testD37_Latency`). The 13 code-generation tests are Incomplete (BLOCKED) without Simulink Coder.
Optional switches, set before `runtests`:

setenv('T06_LONG', '1');            % long drive checks (also T08_LONG, T09_LONG, T17_LONG)
setenv('SHADDAD_SCN_RERUN', '1');   % tScenarios re-simulates instead of reading work/results
`tests/system/tScenarios` evaluates the latest saved results in `work/results`, so it reports the current failures of S2, S6a, S6b and S8b ({tab:tab_c_open}).
